A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GTCA research. All 13 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables, and appendices, support comparison. V1 Appendices A–C are retained as v2 Appendices B–D.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark experiments on Qwen-2.5-7B and Llama-3-8B, structural probing, component ablations, and tree-quality controls.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds training-stage and memory-construction ablations, robustness experiments, and qualitative error analysis.

M1.justification: The default GTCA architecture, cached constituency memory, height-specific projections, 64-chunk limit, gated attention, token mask, and three-stage training remain unchanged. Pre-update/post-update state notation clarifies the existing procedure; the new variants are experimental ablations.

E1.justification: Training datasets and benchmark coverage remain unchanged. Appendix F adds distinct input conditions: meaning-preserving grammatical transformations of CLOTH questions and punctuation, typo, and whitespace noise on MMLU questions.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds the Stage 1 then Stage 3 comparator. Appendix Table 1 adds shared-projection, learned-pooling, and 32/128-chunk comparison variants. Backbone, LoRA-only, and Direct-Joint remain the main baselines, including in the new robustness experiments.

E3.justification: Existing training settings, splits, prompts, and benchmark scoring remain substantively unchanged. New experiments introduce paired original/perturbed evaluation on 1,000 questions per benchmark, prediction-consistency measurement, and controlled component variations. Section 4.1 also reports a length-normalized scoring check.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: skipping Stage 2, varying projection sharing, pooling and memory size, measuring option-score-gap stability, checking length-normalized rankings, examining five BLiMP failures, and testing grammatical perturbations and surface noise. These address design choices and failure modes beyond v1's retained ablations.

E5.justification: V1 reports five-run means without significance annotations. V2 introduces paired-test significance with Holm–Bonferroni correction at p < 0.05 across Tables 3–6. Both versions already specify five runs and different seeds; an increase in runs is not reported. Exact test types and comparison pairings remain unspecified.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores and Figure 3's UUAS curves are unchanged, but substantial new results appear. These include skip-Stage-2 BLiMP accuracy of 82.12, masked/unmasked option-gap changes of 0.013/0.021, and Appendix Tables 1, 4, and 5. GTCA obtains 80.42 perturbed CLOTH accuracy and 71.10 noisy MMLU accuracy under the newly reported conditions.

T1.justification: The method's mathematical definitions, Equations (1)–(11), and coefficient warm-up formula retain their substance. Renaming the mask and distinguishing pre-update/post-update states clarify notation and explanation. No new theoretical assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: checkpoint-compatible syntax injection through GTCA, stabilization through masking and staged training, and improved syntactic performance while preserving broader competence. Added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of complementary training-stage roles, residual reliance on local cues in filler-gap and island errors, and stability under mildly degraded inputs. Appendix A adds design-tradeoff explanations, although its shared-projection and learned-pooling CoLA interpretations contradict the table. The original limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository URL, identifies Qwen-2.5-7B and deterministic settings for the retained coefficient search, and documents settings for new experiments. It also corrects the WinoGrande prompt placeholder. Existing hardware, software versions, parameter counts, and compute-budget disclosures are retained; repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: The cited works and bibliography are unchanged. Related-work edits preserve the same positioning relative to syntax injection, structural probing, parameter-efficient adaptation, and gated attention.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammar, capitalization, terminology, and notation-explanation edits; expands affiliations and contact information; and adds ethics and acknowledgment sections. New appendix sections shift existing appendix labels, while the main narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 clarifies residual-update flow, and Figure 2 labels intermediate quantities. Tables 3–6 gain significance annotations, Table 5 gains a row, and three new appendix tables are added. Existing displays are repositioned and appendix tables renumbered; the overall layout and UUAS plot are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 provides direct answer-stability tests, additional design controls, and failure examples that better support and qualify the unchanged robustness claims. The code URL and statistical reporting also improve transparency. These gains are tempered by unspecified paired-test details and erroneous Appendix A interpretations: shared projection raises CoLA from 56.59 to 56.90, while learned pooling lowers it to 56.04 despite the claimed improvement. The net gain is useful but limited.
